name: sqlgen
listed_description: A reflection-based ORM and SQL query generator for C++-20, similar to Python's SQLAlchemy/SQLModel or Rust's Diesel.
reason: README, repo tree (no benchmark directory), issue search for 'benchmark' (0 results) and WebSearch found no numbers against any baseline; the only performance statement is the feature bullet 'High Performance: Efficient batch operations and prepared statements'. The docs site (munich-data-engineering.github.io) is a blocked *.github.io host and could not be opened. Directional claim only.

name: sqlite_modern_cpp
listed_description: Header only C++14 wrapper around sqlite library.
reason: README has no numbers; the only performance statement is that reusing statements 'might increase the performance significantly' without measurements. No benchmark directory; issue search for 'performance' (6 results: #200, #167, #154, #120, #82, #60) shows no timing numbers in titles; WebSearch for a wrapper shootout found none.

name: sqlite_orm
listed_description: SQLite ORM light header only library for modern C++.
reason: README 'Comparison with other C++ libs' table compares features, not speed; only claim is 'no runtime overhead' for compile-time conditions with no measurements. No benchmark directory; issue searches for 'benchmark' (#1161, #796) and 'performance' (#243, a MSVC warning) hold no timing numbers; WebSearch found no third-party shootout including it. Licence is AGPL-3.0 or paid MIT.

name: SQLiteC++
listed_description: SQLiteC++ (SQLiteCpp) is a smart and easy to use C++ SQLite3 wrapper.
reason: README states design goals 'to be light and fast' and 'no overhead above the SQLite library itself, by design, for lightness and speed' with no measurements. No benchmark directory; issue search for 'benchmark' (PR #363) and 'performance' (10 results, e.g. #178 precompute indices, which holds no timing numbers) shows no numbers. Directional claim only.

name: sqlitemap
reason: README (readme.md) has no benchmark and no comparison to std::map; it only notes autocommit is off by default 'for performance'. 9 stars, 57 commits, no benchmark directory. A persistent SQLite-backed map is not claimed to be faster than std::map; WebSearch found no third-party numbers.

name: sqlpp11
listed_description: A type safe embedded domain specific language for SQL queries and results in C++.
reason: README has no performance numbers or benchmark directory. Only numeric item found is an internal refactor, not a comparison with a competing library or with SQLite: PR #520 (merged Sep 7, 2023) 'Replace regex-based date/time parsing with manual parser' timed 500,000 iterations of timestamp+date parsing, std::regex-based parser vs new hand parser: GCC 13.1.1 -O3 0.923286 s vs 0.00733141 s (about 126x, derived from page data), Clang 16.0.6 -O3 0.944003 s vs 0.0189532 s, VC++ 2019 release 7.97533 s vs 0.074008 s, with -O0 rows about 20x; CPU and OS not stated. The baseline is sqlpp11's own previous parser, so no record written; issue #476 (batch inserts) gives only an anecdote that sqlpp11 was 'considerably faster' than an unnamed library, no numbers. The maintainer notes sqlpp11 is in maintenance mode (migrating to sqlpp23).
